Kant generalized Hume’s problems of induction and causation into a problem about how these judgements are possible. 5+7=12 is an example of this type of judgement, which does not rely on experience but has a predicate that is not contained in its subject.

bonuses.leadin: An essay defending this medium was written in response to Stephen Gosson’s The School of Abuse. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this medium, whose creators are called “the unacknowledged legislators of the world” at the end of an essay titled “A Defense of [this medium].”
This poet of “Ode To the West Wind” and “Ozymandias” wrote “A Defense of Poetry.”

Shelley’s essay was greatly inspired by this other author’s The Defence of Poesy. A character whose name means “star lover” pursues a character whose name means “star” in this Elizabethan poet’s sonnet sequence Astrophil and Stella.

bonuses.leadin: Though Genghis was by far its best-known leader, the Mongol Empire would not reach its territorial peak until decades after his death in 1227. For 10 points each:
parts: This dynasty was founded by Genghis’s grandson Kublai Khan and lasted just under a century until its decline during the Red Turban Rebellion. Marco Polo’s journey to China occurred during this dynasty.
Another grandson of Genghis was this founder of the Ilkhanate. As a general, he commanded a 1258 sack of Baghdad that marked the end of the Islamic Golden Age.

Kublai and Hūlāgū were both sons of this general, the youngest legitimate son of Genghis. Although he never became Khan, this general’s widow Sorghaghtani maneuvered their sons into taking over the Mongol Empire.

bonuses.leadin: Several “luminous blue” stars with this property were documented by Edwin Hubble and Allan Sandage in the 1950s. For 10 points each:
parts: Per the kappa mechanism, compression of the atmosphere of stars with what property causes their opacity to increase? The luminosity of a class of stars with this property can be found using a relation formulated by Henrietta Swan Leavitt.

In many cases, these stars evolve from luminous blue variables. These stars, which have three classes based on CNO spectra, are characterized by their ability to decompose at a rate in excess of 10 to the negative 5 solar masses per year.
Luminous blue variables were originally catalogued as these events since the stars’ “great eruptions” are intensely luminous. Stars can collapse into a black hole following these explosive events.

bonuses.leadin: Festivals celebrated in this region include Galungan, which celebrates the victory of Dharma over Adharma, and a festival celebrating pura temples named Odalan. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this region, where festival days are tracked using the Pawukon calendar. An empty throne atop pillars in this region’s temples represents Acintya (“AH-chin-tee-ah”), this region’s supreme deity.
Devotion to Acintya amongst Balinese Hindus is emphasized in order to comply with this first precept of Pancasila (“pan-cha-SEE-lah”). In Islam, the term tawhid refers to this belief.

Indonesian Hindus avoid breaking Indonesian law by asserting that Acintya and this supreme reality in Hinduism are one, thus making Hinduism monotheistic. Adi Shankara asserted that this concept and Atman are one.

bonuses.leadin: The Sandell–Kolthoff reaction can be adapted to measure the amount of this halogen’s anion in urine. For 10 points each:
parts: A deficiency of what halogen in humans can lead to hypothyroidism and goiter?

In the S–K reaction, iodide-catalyzed reduction of ceric ions turns urine less yellow; that colorimetric change can be assessed using this technique. Beer’s law is used to calculate a sample’s absorbance in this technique.

Before being loaded into a spectrophotometer, reduced S–K samples are subjected to heat and persulfate in this technique. In this technique, a matrixed sample is converted into a solution for elemental analysis.

bonuses.leadin: In one book in this genre, biracial author James McBride recounts the abusive upbringing experienced by his Jewish mother Ruth. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this literary genre exemplified by McBride’s The Color of Water. This genre consists of a real-life author narrating an account of their own life.

This autobiography’s biracial author discusses his experience attending a private Hawaiian preparatory school after being enrolled by his white mother. This autobiography’s title figure died in a car accident in Kenya.

In this autobiography, biracial South African comedian Trevor Noah recounts the “Old Testament discipline” of his mother Patricia, who is shot by Noah’s abusive stepfather at the end of this autobiography.

bonuses.leadin: In a letter to his father, this man explained that he entered a religious order because he “could not stand the great wickedness of the blind people of Italy.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Dominican friar whose followers, the Piagnoni, supported moralistic campaigns like the Bonfire of the Vanities. After a trial by fire was stopped by rain, this man lost popular support and was executed in 1498.
Savonarola briefly ruled this city in Tuscany. Before Savonarola took power, this city’s politics were dominated by members of the Medici family.

Savonarola lived in and preached from this Florentine convent, which was attacked by a mob after the failure of the trial. This convent was reopened as a national museum following Italian independence.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about how tariffs affect foreign policy through economic statecraft, for 10 points each.
parts: Tariffs must satisfy the principles of this organization with a three-letter initialism that regulates commerce between countries.

Mercosur is an example of this type of trade bloc in international economics, wherein countries agree to increase mobility of labor and capital within their borders and share a common external tariff on other countries.

Tariffs are used in import substitution industrialization, which is done by nations undergoing this process. “Inclusive” and “extractive” institutions explain differing levels of this process according to Why Nations Fail.

bonuses.leadin: In this novel, the postman Valuska arranges drunk bar patrons into a replica of the solar system at the Peafeffer tavern. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this apocalyptically-bleak novel, in which the Prince leads a mob against a small town where a mysterious circus exhibits a large whale corpse.
This author wrote The Melancholy of Resistance, as well as Sátántangó, both of which contain his signature very long paragraphs. This Hungarian author won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature.

Krasznahorkai’s grandfather changed his surname from Korin due to this event, which is indirectly referenced in Krasznahorkai’s novel War and War. In Imre Kertész’s novel Fatelessness, Gyuri is sent to Auschwitz during this event.

bonuses.leadin: Five angels watch Mary write a canticle with her right hand in a 1481 painting created in this format titled Madonna of the Magnificat. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this format of painting that likely developed from birthing tray paintings called desco da parto. Paintings in this format are characteristically circular in shape.
The tondo Madonna of the Magnificat was by this Florentine artist of Primavera and The Birth of Venus.
In Botticelli’s Madonna of the Magnificat, Mary’s left hand holds one of these objects. In a 20th-century painting, a fish vomiting out a tiger is expelled from one of these objects.

bonuses.leadin: The Legality Campaign ensured that this politician succeeded Jânio Quadros as president. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this politician who served as vice president under Quadros and Juscelino Kubitschek. This politician was overthrown by Olímpio Mourão Filho in a 1964 coup d’état.
Goulart was the last president of the “Fourth Republic” of this South American country. Later presidents of this country include Fernando Cardoso and Lula da Silva.

The climax of Brazil’s military dictatorship was a period known by this three-word phrase. This three-word phrase also refers to a period in Italy during which Aldo Moro was killed by the Red Brigades.

bonuses.leadin: These fish migrate to upstream freshwater streams in namesake runs. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these fish whose Pacific-residing genera include the sockeye, chinook, and coho species.
Salmon follow this migratory behavior since they are born in freshwater, swim to the ocean, and return to freshwater for breeding.
Anadromous migration is also exhibited by many of these fish, which are the intended targets of the pesticide TFM. These fish and hagfish are the two extant members of the jawless fish clade.

bonuses.leadin: A settler of this colony named Cecily Jordan Farrar was one of the most successful planters, managing a 450-acre plantation called Jordan’s Journey. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this English colony in present-day Virginia that pioneered tobacco planting under John Rolfe.
Cecily maintained her plantation during a surprise attack led by this Native American people group, which established a Confederacy under a namesake leader, who was Pocahontas’s father.

William Farrar, who married Cecily after the first breach of promise in the colonial U.S., operated a 100-acre property along a river with this name. At a place with this name, Ely Parker was told, “I’m glad to see one real American here.”

bonuses.leadin: In one tale from this region, a tiger fails to become human when they can’t live off mugwort and garlic in a cave for a hundred days. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this region. In another myth, Gija flees the Shang dynasty to this region, where he would found the dynasty of Gojoseon.
Korean sources attribute the founding of Gojoseon to this mythical prince, the son of Hwanung and Ungnyeo.
Ungnyeo was one of these creatures who became human after succeeding in the challenge the tiger failed. The Ainu sacrifice one of these creatures during the Iomante ceremony.

bonuses.leadin: Violins marked con sordini open the second movement of this symphony with an F major sarabande, while its finale features a five-part fugato. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this final Mozart symphony in C major nicknamed for a Roman god.
The first movement of the Jupiter Symphony has this musical form. This form was developed from the rounded binary form and was commonly used for first movements in the early Classical period.

Two answers required. In the Jupiter Symphony’s first movement exposition, these two instruments play a contrapuntal motif over the first theme that begins with a half note octave leap, then a descending scale of staccato eighth notes. Mozart adapted a C major concerto for one of these instruments into a D major concerto for the other.

bonuses.leadin: A clown states that this object “shows that incredible meetings do happen,” to which its giver replies that it “deserves pity,” having “fallen from a heaven hard to earn.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this object that is lost when the title character of a play crosses a river, causing Dusyanta to forget her existence.
Dusyanta is cursed to forget the title character in The Recognition of Shakuntala, a play written by Kalidasa in this classical Indian language.
This title protagonist of another Kalidasa play affirms her love for the king by writing a letter on a birch leaf. She is banished from heaven after missing a cue during a performance.

bonuses.leadin: In October 2021, Sandra Mason was elected by this country’s Parliament as its first President. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this country, which transitioned to a republic in November 2021. In a speech at the handover ceremony, then-Prince Charles quoted from Of Age and Innocence, a work by this country’s novelist George Lamming.

Barbadian republicanism gained ground in the fallout of a scandal with this name, in which Commonwealth citizens from the West Indies were wrongly deported from the UK. Those immigrants are part of a “Generation” named after an ocean liner.
Before being elected as President, Mason represented this monarch as Governor General. After her death in 2022, this queen’s son Charles III (“the third”) ascended the throne.

bonuses.leadin: Rings with this property satisfy the ascending chain condition, where any ascending chain of ideals is eventually constant. For 10 points each:
parts: What property named for a German mathematician is possessed by rings with every ideal finitely generated? Given the axiom of choice, this property is equivalent to every set of ideals containing a maximal element.

This mathematician names a basis theorem that states that if a ring is Noetherian, then so is the ring of functions over that ring. This mathematician also published a set of 20 axioms for Euclidean geometry.

Hilbert’s basis theorem is often proved by considering the set of these parameters for some polynomials, the largest exponent of any variable for a single-variable polynomial. This parameter is two for quadratic polynomials.

bonuses.leadin: This man pursued a diplomatic rapprochement between France and the Ayutthaya (“a-yoo-ta-ya”) Kingdom, angering his former employer, the British East India Company. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this politician who served as chief minister to the Ayutthaya king Narai the Great. After Narai was overthrown by his cousin Phetracha, this Greek-born adventurer was gruesomely executed.
Phaulkon shaped foreign policy in the Ayutthaya Kingdom, which ruled over this modern-day country. Since 1782, this modern-day country has been ruled by ten kings named Rama from the Chakri dynasty.

The Ayutthaya Kingdom was destroyed after a series of invasions from this neighboring dynasty. Ava and Mandalay were capitals of this final Burmese dynasty, which succeeded the Toungoo and was annexed by the British Empire in 1885.

bonuses.leadin: This concept’s namesake “hard problem” is a foundational topic in the philosophy of mind. For 10 points each:
parts: What concept sometimes explained in terms of “qualia” is described by Thomas Nagel as “what it is like to be” something?
This kind of hypothetical being popularized by David Chalmers is behaviourally identical to humans but lacks qualia.

In an argument against p-zombies, this thinker posited zimbos, who have second-order representational states. He also used a thought experiment involving coffee tasters to criticize the existence of qualia in “Quining Qualia.”

bonuses.leadin: Santu Mofokeng documented overcrowded transportation conditions resulting from this policy in the photobook Train Churches. For 10 points each:
parts: The bloody aftermath of a demonstration protesting what South African racial policy was photographed by Sam Nzima during the Soweto uprising?

In 1949, this photographer shot an image of two shirtless African gold miners while stationed in apartheid-era South Africa. Another image by this photographer shows a line of flood victims standing in front of a billboard depicting an affluent family.

Apartheid was also documented by Kevin Carter, who was better known for an image of a girl affected by one of these events. That image depicting one of these events also features a vulture in its midground.

bonuses.leadin: Tumbling of a rotating ellipsoid-shaped one of these objects can be visualized using Poinsot’s (“pwahn-SOH’s”) construction. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these solid objects that maintain their shape when a force attempts to deform them.

In Poinsot’s construction, this pseudovector quantity traces onto the rigid body to generate its polhode. A reference frame’s Euler acceleration equals the cross product of the negative time derivative of this quantity and vector position.
This quantity denoted tau is assumed not to act on a rigid body in Poinsot’s construction. This quantity is the rotational analog of linear force.

bonuses.leadin: In Great Expectations, Compeyson and Abel Magwitch spend time in one of these locations before departing and encountering Pip. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these places. One of these places named Newgate was frequently depicted in British novels of the early 19th century, and Oscar Wilde wrote about the execution of Charles Woolridge in a ballad titled for one of these places named Reading (“RED-ing”).
This character was born a prisoner in Newgate after her mother “pleaded her belly.” This character, who was “five times a wife,” inherits a farm in Maryland at the end of a novel by Daniel Defoe.
A lookalike English gentleman is crowned king of Ruritania after a former ruler is drugged in The Prisoner of Zenda, a novel by this author of The Heart of Princess Osra.
